jobs.title: Managing Director
jobs.description:
What does it take to turn a talent business into a high-performing growth engine?

At TalentoHC, we’re looking for a senior leader who can see the bigger picture, build exceptional teams, and turn commercial opportunities into measurable business results.

You’ll shape growth strategy, strengthen strategic customer partnerships, develop a high-performing recruiting organization, and take ownership of the business performance and financial health of the practice.

If you’re ready to lead with vision, build with purpose, and create lasting business impact
, we’d love to meet you!

MEET THE ROLE: YOUR PURPOSE:

Senior 360° leadership role responsible for driving the growth, performance, people leadership, and profitability of a customer-aligned Talent Practice.
The role combines business development, strategic customer partnership, recruiting expertise, and team leadership to deliver high-value talent solutions and sustainable business results.
Accountable for the full business cycle, from identifying and developing new opportunities to expanding existing customer relationships, leading recruiting teams, and ensuring successful delivery of complex talent engagements. The Practice Manager also owns the financial performance of the practice, leveraging market insight, commercial acumen, operational discipline, and people leadership to maximize revenue, gross profit, productivity, and profitability.

WHERE YOU’LL MAKE YOUR MARK:

Drive Business Development:
Identify, develop, and convert new business opportunities by building strategic prospect relationships, understanding market needs, and positioning Talento’s capabilities to win new customer partnerships and generate sustainable and profitable growth.
Expand Customer Partnerships :
Strengthen and grow existing customer relationships by uncovering unmet talent needs, expanding the scope of searches and services, and developing account strategies that increase retention, share of wallet, and long-term customer value.
Lead the Team:
Lead, coach, and develop a high-performing recruiting team, including junior talent, by setting clear expectations, driving accountability, allocating resources, and building capabilities that improve team productivity and delivery.
Own Practice Performance & P&L:
Drive the overall performance and profitability of the practice with direct accountability for revenue, gross profit, productivity, and profitability, while balancing business growth, customer outcomes, team performance, and operational efficiency.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE:

You’ll be successful when you’re:
Growing the Business
Expanding Strategic Partnerships
Building High-Performing Teams
Delivering Exceptional Talent Outcomes
Driving Profitable Growth

WHAT MAKES YOU THE ONE:

You bring:

EXPERIENCE & EDUCATION:

10+ years of experience in recruiting, executive search, staffing, or talent solutions, with a proven track record owning the full 360° business and recruiting lifecycle—from business development and client partnership to complex searches and successful placements.
5+ years of experience leading, developing, and coaching recruiting professionals.
Demonstrated experience managing team performance, setting priorities, allocating workloads, and developing recruiting capabilities
Experience managing or contributing to practice, business unit, or P&L performance, including revenue, gross profit, forecasting, productivity, and profitability.
2+ years of experience owning complex customer relationships, with a proven track record of growing and expanding accounts through a land-and-expand approach.
Demonstrated experience managing complex high-value searches while maintaining direct accountability for client outcomes.

TECHNICAL KNOWLEDGE:

Talent Market Expertise:
Strong understanding of talent markets, industry dynamics, functional profiles, compensation trends, and talent availability across diverse industries and customer environments.
Complex Search Expertise
: Proven ability to design and execute sophisticated searches for specialized, senior, and difficult-to-fill positions using targeted research, market mapping, and advanced sourcing strategies.
End-to-End Recruiting Expertise:
Strong command of the full recruiting lifecycle, including client intake and calibration, search strategy, sourcing, candidate assessment, engagement, negotiation, closing, and successful placement.
People & Performance Management:
Strong knowledge of recruiting team management, coaching, performance development, workload allocation, productivity management, and capability development.
Market Intelligence:
Ability to leverage talent market data, industry trends, competitor insights, and candidate motivations to provide actionable recommendations and shape effective search strategies.
Business Development & Solution Development:
Strong understanding of consultative business development, including prospecting, client discovery, solution design, proposals, statements of work, pricing, and negotiation within a talent solutions environment.
Commercial & Financial Acumen:
Strong understanding of P&L management, revenue, gross profit, gross margin, forecasting, pipeline management, productivity, resource planning, and the financial drivers of profitable recruiting engagements.
Recruiting Technology & Analytics:
Proficiency with ATS/CRM platforms, LinkedIn Recruiter, sourcing technologies, and recruiting analytics to support both search execution and business performance.

COMPETENCIES & SKILLS:

People Leadership:
Ability to lead, coach, and develop high-performing recruiting teams, including junior talent.
Commercial Acumen: Strong business development, customer partnership, negotiation, and growth mindset.
Financial & Business Ownership:
Ability to manage performance against revenue, profitability, productivity, and P&L objectives.
Strategic Thinking & Decision-Making :
Ability to navigate complex business and talent challenges, prioritize effectively, and make data-driven decisions.
Executive Communication & Influence:
Strong communication, relationship-building, and influencing skills across customers, candidates, and internal stakeholders.

YOUR WELL-BEING MATTERS!

We believe great work starts with feeling supported at work and beyond. That’s why we offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, financial well-being, peace of mind, and everyday life with meaningful benefits for you and your family.
Comprehensive Health Coverage
: Choose from three PPO medical plans through Meritain Aetna, with preventive care covered at 100%.
24/7 Virtual Care:
Get free, unlimited access to Teladoc for general medical care, mental health support, and more—wherever you are.
No-Cost Surgical & Imaging Services:
Access eligible surgical procedures and diagnostic imaging with no out-of-pocket costs through Valenz Health.
Dental & Vision Coverage
: Access Guardian dental and vision plans for you and your family, including orthodontic coverage.
Life, AD&D & Disability Insurance:
Receive basic life, AD&D, and short- and long-term disability coverage at no cost to you.
Retirement Savings:
Build toward your financial future with a 401(k) plan and automatic enrollment.
HSA & FSA:
Take advantage of tax-advantaged Health Savings and Flexible Spending Accounts to help manage eligible healthcare expenses.
Employee Assistance Program:
Access confidential counseling and well-being resources 24/7 for you and your family.
Pet Benefits:
Enjoy veterinary discounts, 24/7 pet telehealth, and additional resources for your furry family members.
Legal Support:
Get unlimited access to legal advice, document review, and complimentary will preparation.
Commuter Benefits:
Save with pre-tax benefits on eligible commuting and transit expenses.

jobs.title: Managing Director - Accounting Advisory (Operational Accounting/Controller)
jobs.description:
From the beginning, our goal was to establish an advisory firm that stands apart from the rest – one that is grounded in our Core Values and dedicated to creating a positive experience not just for our clients, but for our people too. We firmly believe in the strength of collaboration, enthusiasm, generosity, and perseverance as the driving forces behind our success. With advisory solutions spanning accounting and risk, technology-enabled transformation, and transactions, we partner with our clients to solve today’s challenges and deliver present and future value.

Our commitment to our people has earned us numerous awards including Inc5000's Fastest Growing Companies and Glassdoor's Best Places to Work. Explore what our employees have to say about our unique culture by clicking here.

By joining our rapidly growing Accounting Advisory practice, you will serve as a trusted partner to our clients across a broad range of industries, company stages, and sizes, including early-stage, emerging growth, middle-market, and large, complex organizations. Our work spans both public and private companies, with significant exposure to Private Equity-backed portfolio companies. You will bring your first-hand experience, unique perspectives, and functional knowledge to deliver tailored, integrated solutions that help our clients solve today's challenges and set the foundation for future success. As a Managing Director at CrossCountry Consulting, you will be responsible for a mix of client delivery, business development, leading teams, and developing junior team members, as well as serving as a member of CrossCountry's leadership team.

What You'll Do

General Accounting Close Support:

Lead and oversee the development of streamlined monthly close processes for clients, including cash-to-accrual conversions and creation of supporting schedules
Validate the existence of assets and prepare associated roll forwards
Review and oversee balance sheet reconciliations (intercompany, inventory, cash, prepaids, etc.)
Support various aspects of accounting compliance, including tax forms, sales tax exemptions, 1099s, etc., while contributing to the preparation of financial statements and development of internal controls and policies
Oversee preparation of budgets or forecasts and develop reports for management or regulatory bodies
Guide the implementation of cloud-based finance and accounting systems
Manage and review journal entries, invoices, and reconciliation of accounts during monthly or annual closings
Guide companies through efficient external audit processes

Financial Reporting Support

Support SEC filing, design of reporting processes, restatement assistance, and traditional 10-K, 10-Q, and 8-K filings
Conduct IPO-readiness assessments and assist clients in preparation for a public offering (via Form S-1 or F-1)
Advise clients on complex accounting standards (US GAAP and/or IFRS), including revenue recognition, lease accounting, derivatives, business combinations, and consolidation
Oversee and improve financial planning and analysis (budgeting, forecasting, data analysis)
Review monthly internal financial reporting packs and monthly regulatory reporting

Operations Support

Liaise with business units outside of accounting to integrate business operations
Advise clients on leveraging AI and automation tools to streamline close processes, improve forecasting, and enhance data-driven decision making
Partner with IT teams to integrate financial systems during acquisitions
Transform finance and/or accounting functions, including accounting and operational process improvements, integration support, target operating model decisions, and RBA/Data Analytics

Client Delivery

Responsible for account leadership and financial management of multiple accounts and sustained relationships with senior client executives
Assist with complex transactions, technical accounting standard and policy implementations, and operational accounting engagements

Practice Leadership: Serve as a key leader in the Accounting Advisory practice by:

Oversee client accounts, projects, and engagements, including work plans, staffing, timelines, fee negotiations, and budgets throughout all lifecycle phases
Build and grow high-level relationships and networks with clients across the West Coast market
Generate sustainable, repeatable revenue through new clients and growth at existing clients
Develop timely resolutions to issues, risks, and project team conflicts
Manage the full life cycle of proposals from development to deal closure
Develop delivery methodologies and new service offerings
Contribute to developing and implementing firm-approved, AI-enabled solutions for clients, in accordance with company policies on data protection, intellectual property, and professional standards
Act as role model, supervisor, coach, and mentor to team members
Ensure staffing and recruiting needs are met across clients and the West Coast market

What You'll Bring

15+ years of related experience spanning advisory and controllership roles for commercial or PE-backed portfolio companies, supported by a strong foundation in professional services (public accounting, advisory firm, or management consulting firm)
7+ years of hands-on Controllership experience in emerging growth, middle market, and/or PE-backed portfolio companies (Software/SaaS or Healthcare, or broad B2B industry exposure preferred)
Deep expertise in operational accounting, including month-end close, financial reporting, reconciliations, and internal controls
In-depth knowledge of accounting standards (US GAAP and/or IFRS)
Hands-on experience - OR - significant exposure to ERP systems and tools such as: NetSuite, Sage, MS Dynamics, QuickBooks, Workiva, DFIN, Tableau, PowerBI, Alteryx, Snowflake, SQL, Python
Ability to leverage AI and automation to optimize accounting processes, enhance reporting accuracy, and drive operational efficiency
Consistent track record of building and developing strong client relationships in the West Coast market
Personal brand, executive presence, integrity, collaborative nature, poise and polish under pressure
Demonstrated ability to responsibly explore and adopt firm-approved AI tools to enhance productivity and innovation
Proven track record as an influential change agent, championing and successfully implementing new ideas and initiatives
Passion for mentoring and leading teams while efficiently implementing new ideas and initiatives
Identify new growth and shared revenue opportunities, collaborating with sales leadership to originate new business and grow existing relationships

Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field
CPA or CA certification preferred
Based in or willing to relocate to California; ability to serve clients across the West Coast market
As one might expect, travel is innate in some of our projects. With that said, our approach to travel is a thoughtful, meaningful one and we do our best to avoid scheduling back-to-back extended travel projects. Even so, travel will vary project-to-project based on client preferences and may sometimes come in bursts.

For applicants located in California State, CrossCountry Consulting is required to include an estimate of the compensation range for this role. The following range takes into account a wide range of factors including but not limited to, skills, experience, education, licenses, certifications, business needs, and internal equity. An estimate of the current range is $281,750 - $402,500 + annual bonus + additional benefits.

Benefits Summary

The CrossCountry total rewards package includes comprehensive healthcare options, including medical, dental, and vision coverage; flexible spending accounts; and a 401(k) with company matching. Additionally, employees can take advantage of generous parental and maternity leave policies, technology stipends, and wellness reimbursement programs, all designed to support both professional growth and personal well-being. For detailed information about benefits at CrossCountry, please visit our dedicated benefits site: https://www.crosscountry-consulting.com/careers/benefits/.

CrossCountry provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment and believes that respect and fair treatment are critical to creating a productive and inclusive workplace.

As an equal opportunity employer, CrossCountry is fully committed to comply with all federal, state, and local laws and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability, pregnancy, genetics, sexual orientation, veteran status, gender identity or expression or any other protected characteristic. jobs.description:
ABOUT STEPHEN SILVER FINE JEWELRY:

For over 40 years, Stephen Silver Fine Jewelry has remained rooted in the San Francisco Bay Area. We are one of America’s premier jewelers dedicated to sharing our expertise in rare gemstones, custom jewelry design, and new and pre-owned luxury timepieces.
At Stephen Silver, you will join a visionary team of talent builders and one of the world’s premier jewelry and watch houses. We believe our role is to serve and guide our customers through their journey of discovering the world's hidden treasures. We strive to create the pinnacle of a high-touch and personal customer experience. You will work with clientele and products that define the most exclusive side of the glittering world of the ultra-high-end watches and jewelry space.

ABOUT THE POSITION:

We are currently seeking a highly organized, detail-oriented Executive Assistant to join our team. This role requires a proactive approach, excellent problem-solving skills, and the ability to maintain high levels of confidentiality. The ideal candidate will demonstrate a blend of professionalism, communication proficiency, and the capacity to manage multiple tasks efficiently.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

Provide 24/7 availability
when the executive is traveling to ensure seamless communication and support.
Manage and coordinate executives’ calendars, scheduling appointments and meetings to optimize their time.
Open and prepare the CEO and President's offices in the morning, tidy and close the office at the end of the day.
Handle all aspects of travel arrangements, including bookings, restaurant reservations, itinerary planning, and coordination of transportation and accommodation.
Type, prepare, and review various documents, including e-mails, reports, memos, letters, and others.
Answer phone calls, direct calls to appropriate parties, or take messages as necessary.
Record, type, and distribute minutes from meetings, ensuring all participants have access to necessary information.
Manage, track, and inventory wine cellar and tequila/liquor storage.
Greet visitors with professionalism, determining access to appropriate individuals within the organization.
Read and analyze incoming memos, submissions, and reports; determine their significance and plan distribution accordingly.
Oversee general office duties, including ordering supplies, maintaining records management database systems, and ensuring operational efficiency.
Assist with facility and human resources issues, offering support and coordination as needed.
Maintain corporate documents, records, and reports, ensuring effective filing and retrieval systems.
Manage incoming correspondence, including faxes and emails, sorting, and distributing as required.
Back up and manage other Administrative and Office Administrative Staff responsibilities as needed and to assure coverage for absences.
Perform other duties and responsibilities as assigned to support the executive and organizational needs.
Manage and account for CEO and/or Presidents expenses, which includes the Madera restaurant reconciliation.
Manage storage units, keys, access, and agreements.
Cover and back up for Office Administrator and/or Front Desk duties, such as phone, mail, deliveries, etc.
Manager all former EA email accounts / in boxes so information is accounted for until it is decided not to be needed.
Handle personal assistance duties such as running errands to assist the President and CEO’s with personal responsibilities.
Other duties as assigned by CEO and/or President.

Competencies:

Communication Proficiency:
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
Time Management:
Ability to prioritize tasks and manage time effectively.
Collaboration Skills:
Capable of working well with others and contributing to a positive team environment.
Personal Effectiveness/Credibility:
Maintains a professional demeanor and exercises discretion.
Flexibility:
Adaptable to changing priorities and demands.
Technical Capacity:
Proficient in office software and technology tools.
Stress Management/Composure:
Capable of working under pressure while maintaining a calm demeanor.
Teamwork Orientation:
Works collaboratively to achieve shared goals.

QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma/GED or equivalent required; associate degree or bachelor’s degree a plus.
A minimum of five years of experience in an administrative or executive assistant role.
Demonstrated ability to handle confidential information with discretion.
Highly proficient in MS Office applications and comfortable learning new software and systems.
Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, time management, and problem-solving capabilities.
Excellent communication skills both verbal and written

This role is pivotal to the smooth operation of our executive functions and offers the opportunity to contribute significantly to our organizational goals. We encourage you to apply and join our dynamic team if you possess the qualifications, experience, and competencies listed above.

WHY JOIN THIS COMPANY:

Fast Paced, High performing, caring, fun and dynamic team
A culture focused on well-being, innovation, and growth
Generous salary & bonus: Base Pay salary with a high bonus potential
Incredible benefits: Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Flexible Time Off, Holiday pay, winter break closure, 401K and pension after 1-year vesting, and other various company-related perks like daily lunches.

Working Conditions
This job operates in a professional office environment. It routinely uses standard office equipment such as computers, phones, photocopiers, filing cabinets, and fax machines. Evening and weekend work may be required. This is an onsite position M-F.

Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that an employee must meet to perform the essential functions of this job successfully. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to sit, use hands to finger, handle, or feel, and reach with hands and arms. The employee must be able to talk and hear to communicate effectively with staff, supervisors, vendors, and the public. This is a largely sedentary role; however, some filing is required. This would require the ability to lift files, open filing cabinets, and bend or stand as necessary.

jobs.title: Associate Executive Director
jobs.description:
Position Summary The Associate Executive Director, SEIT / Pendency Programs is the senior second-in-command to the Executive Director and is responsible for translating executive strategy into disciplined day-to-day execution. The role owns operational performance across intake, service activation, provider deployment, documentation discipline, family and stakeholder responsiveness, quality assurance, and internal management routines. The Associate Executive Director must be able to operate independently, make sound decisions within delegated authority, and assume leadership of the division when the Executive Director is unavailable.
Mission of the Role To ensure that the SEIT / pendency platform operates with consistency, accountability, compliance, and speed as the organization grows - converting the Executive Director's strategic direction into repeatable operating systems and reliable service delivery.
· Drive excellent execution from referral through service launch and ongoing case management.
· Maintain disciplined provider staffing, deployment, supervision, and performance follow-through.
· Strengthen documentation quality, compliance readiness, and operational controls.
· Create dependable management rhythms, dashboards, escalation pathways, and accountability.
· Protect a high-touch family experience and strong attorney / referral-partner relationships.
· Serve as the Executive Director's trusted operating deputy and succession-capable leadership partner.
Key Responsibilities1. Executive Partnership and Delegated Leadership ·  Serve as the Executive Director's principal operating partner and second-in-command for the SEIT / pendency division.
·  Translate strategic priorities into weekly and monthly operating plans, owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
·  Lead divisional operations during the Executive Director's absence and ensure uninterrupted decision-making and stakeholder responsiveness.
·  Prepare decision briefs, operating updates, risk summaries, and recommendations for the Executive Director and senior leadership.
·  Ensure priorities are cascaded clearly across managers, coordinators, providers, compliance, credentialing, billing, and support functions.
·  Maintain an effective escalation framework so issues are resolved at the lowest appropriate level and material risks reach the Executive Director promptly.
2. SEIT / Pendency Program Operations ·  Own day-to-day execution from referral receipt and intake through documentation collection, case acceptance, provider matching, service activation, ongoing coordination, and service continuity.
·  Standardize operating procedures for intake, scheduling, case assignment, provider communication, follow-up, and exception management.
·  Monitor active cases, pending cases, unfilled mandates, provider availability, geographic coverage, service start dates, and aging queues.
·  Run daily / weekly operating reviews to identify bottlenecks and ensure timely intervention.
·  Coordinate with program leaders to ensure caseloads, staffing, service intensity, and supervision structures remain appropriate as volume grows.
·  Develop contingency plans for provider absences, service interruptions, urgent placements, and high-risk cases.
3. DOE / CPSE / CSE / IEP / Pendency Execution ·  Apply strong practical knowledge of NYC DOE-facing workflows, CPSE / CSE processes, IEP implementation, mandated services, school coordination, and documentation expectations.
·  Ensure operational teams understand case-specific service requirements and translate those requirements into accurate provider assignments and service plans.
·  Oversee service continuity and case-transition execution for pendency matters, including coordination with families, attorneys, schools, and providers.
·  Identify documentation gaps, authorization issues, scheduling barriers, or provider shortages that could delay mandated service delivery.
·  Escalate matters with legal, regulatory, reputational, or significant financial implications to the Executive Director while driving the operational work needed to resolve them.
4. Provider Recruitment, Onboarding, Deployment, and Performance ·  Manage the operating execution of the provider strategy, including recruiting pipeline visibility, screening coordination, credential completion, onboarding readiness, assignment, and retention.
·  Ensure provider assignments reflect credentials, student needs, geography, schedule, language needs, availability, and service expectations.
·  Track time-to-onboard, time-to-placement, fill rate, provider utilization, cancellations, service gaps, and retention.
·  Strengthen provider orientation, training, supervision, communication standards, and field support.
·  Address provider performance concerns in partnership with program leadership, HR, compliance, and the Executive Director as appropriate.
·  Build a professional provider culture centered on quality, reliability, communication, and documentation discipline.

Required Qualifications · Minimum 7 years of progressive leadership or management experience in SEIT, preschool special education, pendency-related services, CPSE / CSE programs, special-education operations, or a closely related NYC educational / human-services environment.
· Demonstrated success managing multi-step service operations, teams, providers, and performance in a regulated environment.
· Strong working knowledge of NYC special education systems, DOE-facing workflows, IEP-based service implementation, documentation requirements, and provider assignment realities.
· Experience managing operational escalations involving families, providers, schools, attorneys, advocates, or referral partners.
· Demonstrated ability to build and enforce SOPs, management routines, performance standards, and quality controls.
· Strong analytical, organizational, written, and verbal communication skills.
· Executive judgment, calm decision-making, high accountability, discretion, and the ability to operate with limited supervision.
Education, Credentials, and NYC-Specific Experience Education:
Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree preferred in Special Education, Educational Leadership, Early Childhood Education, School Administration, Social Work, Public Administration, Healthcare Administration, Business / Operations, or a related field.
Preferred Credentials:

The CDO will spearhead dynamic revenue growth and ongoing sustainable through: (1) management of a portfolio of leadership-level donors; (2) engaging leadership—especially the CEO—to greatest impact in those leadership-level relationships; and (3) strategically activating the External Affairs team. The CDO will work cross-functionally to build Harlem Grown’s brand and elevate storytelling. This position requires a seasoned professional with a deep understanding of nonprofit development, a proven track record of leading dynamic revenue growth, and a passion for Harlem Grown. By fostering relationships with donors and stewarding their engagement, the CDO will play a pivotal role in advancing Harlem Grown's mission and driving its continued growth.

The CDO will personally manage a portfolio of approximately 25 high-capacity donors with the potential to give $100,000 or more annually — closing six- and seven-figure gifts — while providing oversight and accountability for the full advancement team of 3–5 professionals. Revenue Accountability & Fundraising Leadership

The Executive Director (ED) is responsible for leading the local chapter to achieve program objectives, fundraising targets, and managing and growing the annual local budget in alignment with Back on My Feet's Four Strategic Anchors:  We Drive Real Impact, Running Is Our Foundation, We Build Local Roots for Lasting Impact,  and  Our People Are the Movement . The Executive Director is the operational leader of their chapter. They own day-to-day program delivery, local fundraising and development, partner and volunteer relationships, and team performance. Program Strategy, Implementation & Delivery

Own and drive local implementation of the BoMF program model, ensuring running is structurally central to all member touchpoints, from Circle Ups (BOMF’s community based running practice) to workforce development.

Oversee delivery of BoMF's workforce development program; grow and strengthen partnerships with referral agencies, corporate partners, and employment partners to provide members with needed support and services.
Ensure program model fidelity. If running culture drifts, energy erodes, or standards slip, the ED owns the identification and correction of that drift at the local level, in coordination with the VP of Program and Chief Running Officer.
Source and share member stories, outcomes, and program data with national teams on a defined cadence to support organizational reporting, marketing, and donor engagement.

Leadership & Staff Management

Hire, manage, and develop local staff, fostering a collaborative, high-performing environment grounded in BoMF's Strategic Anchors.
Set clear expectations, provide ongoing feedback, and hold staff accountable to program and operational KPIs.
Build a local team culture where running, community, and transformation are not talking points, they are operating principles.
Collaborate with Program leadership on annual goals, performance reviews, and professional development for local staff.

Recruit, train, and retain individual and corporate volunteers to support Circle Ups, workforce development, events, and fundraising goals.

Cultivate and steward relationships with local donors, corporate partners, and foundations.
Identify and secure diverse local funding sources, including grants, individual donors, and corporate sponsorships.
Plan and manage local fundraising events to generate revenue and community awareness, in coordination with the national Partnerships Team.
Collaborate with the Partnerships Team on national partnerships, relationships, and campaigns; ensure neither function commits the other without prior alignment.
Build, engage, and grow the local Advisory Board to advance fundraising, partnerships, and program objectives.

Ensure accurate and timely tracking of program, donor, and partner data in Salesforce to support real-time KPI assessment and organizational reporting.
Manage the local chapter budget, tracking performance against targets, and escalating variances proactively.
Proactively collaborate with BoMF national staff to provide impactful stories and event details for media coverage and donor communications.
Perform other duties as assigned.

You lead locally with ownership.
You treat your chapter like it's yours, because it is. You don't wait for direction from national on day-to-day decisions. You own the outcomes.
You let the Strategic Anchors guide everything you do.
You don't just understand the direction, you build toward it, make decisions through it, and hold your team accountable to it.
You believe in the transformative power of running.
Not as a feature of the program, but as the mechanism through which lives change.

You lead with directness and warmth. You don't confuse kindness with softness, or accountability with harshness.
You bring challenges forward.

You're operationally sharp.
You can hold a budget, manage Salesforce, run a donor meeting, and lead a 5am run, sometimes all in the same day.

Fundraising and/or development experience, comfort cultivating donors, managing a portfolio, and closing local gifts.

Temple University Health System is seeking a physician executive to serve as Chief Executive Officer of Temple Faculty Physicians (TFP)

The CEO is responsible for the overall leadership and performance of TFP and partners closely with the Lewis Katz School of Medicine.

800+ physicians and advanced practice providers
across the full range of medical and surgical specialties
Care delivered at Temple University Hospital, Fox Chase Cancer Center, Jeanes Campus, Episcopal Campus, Chestnut Hill Hospital
, and ambulatory sites throughout the Philadelphia region
Physicians are dually employed by TFP and the Lewis Katz School of Medicine (LKSOM)
, holding faculty appointments while practicing through TFP
A payer mix and acuity profile that demand disciplined, creative physician enterprise leadership — and make that leadership matter

Position Summary

Reporting directly to the President & CEO of Temple University Health System
, the CEO is accountable for TFP's strategic, operational, financial, and cultural performance — clinical operations, financial results, provider compensation and workforce strategy, quality and access, and compliance.
A successful leader in this role is experienced in leading through influence and building effective partnerships with the medical school, department chairs, operational leaders, and all parts of the integrated health system.

Strategic Leadership

Develop a multi-year strategy for TFP aligned with the TUHS strategic plan and LKSOM's academic priorities
Integrate practice plan operations — payer contracting, revenue cycle, access, care standards, shared services — into the broader clinical enterprise while preserving departmental identity
Partner with system leadership on ambulatory growth, network development, service lines, and physician-facing capital investment

Academic Partnership and Governance

Establish a structured, trusted working relationship with the Dean of LKSOM, including a clear framework for joint decisions on funds flow, recruitment, effort allocation, and chair searches
Serve as the principal executive partner to clinical department chairs and co-lead the Council of Chairs
Staff the TFP board and keep governance structures current and effective

Financial Performance

Lead TFP's operating budget, multi-year financial plan, and results
Design and administer a transparent, defensible academic funds flow model
Drive revenue cycle performance and partner on payer strategy, including value-based and risk-bearing arrangements
Build provider- and department-level analytics on productivity, margin, access, and cost

Provider Recruitment, Engagement, and Retention

Oversee physician recruitment strategy jointly with chairs and the Dean's office
Champion faculty wellness, development, and retention
Make the practice plan transparent and legible to the physicians it serves
Build the next generation of physician leaders

Quality, Access, and Patient Experience

Set and achieve access targets — new patient availability, third-next-available, referral capture, continuity
Align TFP incentives to system quality and population health goals
Own patient experience performance across TFP sites
Sponsor ambulatory EHR and digital access strategy: scheduling, telehealth, messaging, provider efficiency

Operations and Organizational Development

Standardize ambulatory operations — staffing, templates, site management — where it improves performance
Develop a TFP leadership team with clear accountability and succession depth
Establish a disciplined operating rhythm with transparent scorecards and closed-loop follow-through

Qualifications

Required

MD or DO from an accredited medical or osteopathic medical school
Progressive executive leadership in a large multispecialty physician group, academic practice plan, or integrated physician enterprise, including P&L accountability
A track record of leading operational and financial improvement, integration, or large-scale change in a complex, matrixed environment
Substantive experience partnering with medical school leadership and clinical department chairs

Preferred

MBA or equivalent business credential
Experience in an academic health system serving a complex urban or safety-net population
Experience with value-based and risk-bearing contracting
Experience leading through governance transition, employment consolidation, or practice plan restructuring
Experience negotiating and administering funds flow between separately governed academic and clinical entities

Temple Health is an academic health system with a deeply rooted mission: exceptional care for a community that needs it, education of the next generation of clinicians, and research that moves medicine forward. The people who thrive here are drawn to hard problems and the belief that disciplined, humane leadership changes outcomes for patients and providers alike. As CEO of TFP, you will have the platform, the partnership, and the mandate to do exactly that.

Temple Faculty Physicians, the academic practice plan of Temple Health, is made up of more than 500 employed physicians who are the cornerstone of clinical care and teaching for Temple's healthcare enterprise. These physicians practice in 20 academic departments encompassing virtually every subspecialty in modern medicine. While remaining committed to our mission of serving patients in our North Philadelphia community, in recent years, Temple Faculty Physicians has expanded its geographic reach beyond Temple University Hospital's Health Sciences campus. Today, Temple faculty physician offices are located at Temple University Hospital and its campuses, satellite offices located in Center City Philadelphia, Fort Washington, PA, Oaks, PA, and various other outpatient settings. jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Director of Strategic Partnerships & Development leads ISTH's efforts to build and diversify non-dues revenue in service of the Society's mission to advance the understanding, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of thrombotic and bleeding disorders worldwide. Reporting to the Executive Director & CEO, the Director will design and build ISTH's strategic partnerships and development function from the ground up, spanning corporate and industry partnerships, sponsorship, education and research support, and institutional giving. The Director will cultivate durable, mission-aligned relationships across a global partner community while establishing a sustainable foundation for long-term growth.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Revenue Diversification

Develop and lead ISTH's strategic partnerships and revenue-diversification strategy, reducing concentration risk across partners, sectors, and revenue types.
Analyze the current revenue mix, benchmark against peer international societies, and set measurable growth and diversification targets.
Build a balanced portfolio of revenue streams impacting areas across annual congress, education, research, policy and awareness, institutional giving.

Corporate & Industry Partnerships

Design and launch a tiered Strategic Partner Program that converts episodic sponsorships into multi-year, year-round relationships.
Cultivate, negotiate, and steward partnerships across pharmaceutical, diagnostics, medical device, and digital-health sectors.
Serve as the senior relationship owner for ISTH's largest corporate partners, engaging in medical-affairs, commercial, and foundation counterparts.

Institutional Giving & Development

Establish a funding pillar including research and fellowship funds, foundation grants, and institutional giving that diversifies beyond corporate support.
Partner with foundations, and intergovernmental/NGO funders (e.g., WHO) on global health and LMIC-access programs.

Grant Writing & Proposal Development

Lead the development of high-quality grant proposals, letters of inquiry, and funding applications to foundations, corporate foundations, and other funders in support of ISTH's research, education, awareness, and global-health priorities.
Translate ISTH initiatives — fellowships, research funds, LMIC-access programs, and priority strategic initiatives — into fundable proposals tailored to each funder's mission, guidelines, and reporting expectations.
Manage the full grants lifecycle: funder prospecting and cultivation, proposal and budget development submission, and post-award stewardship and reporting, in partnership with internal departments.
Partner with program and scientific staff to source proposal content while preserving the scientific-independence firewall for funder-supported programs.

Congress Events & Sponsorships

Develop and maximize Congress-related partnership and sponsorship opportunities, including exhibition, industry-supported symposia, digital and hybrid placements, in close collaboration with the Meetings & Events team.
Develop year-round partnership opportunities around World Thrombosis Day, the Women's Health Initiative, and other mission-aligned platforms in collaboration with public affairs, marketing, education, and other relevant teams.

Compliance, Ethics & Scientific Independence

Uphold and operationalize the scientific-independence firewall so that no funder influences SSC standards, guidelines/guidance, editorial decisions, or the scientific program.
Ensure all relationships comply with the strictest applicable global transparency and disclosure regimes.
Develop and apply grant-acceptance and partner-vetting policies, escalating edge cases through the appropriate governance channels.

Team Leadership & Operations

Build and lead the Strategic Partnerships team through a phased approach aligned with revenue growth and organizational priorities; set goals, coach, and develop staff.
Stand up the function's infrastructure — database, partnership prospectus and rate card, contract and approval workflows, and reporting dashboards.
Own pipeline discipline, forecasting, and impact reporting with support from finance team; ensure relationships are held institutionally.

The Director of Strategic Partnerships & Business Development will be a seasoned leader with demonstrated success in strategic leadership, organizational management, and partnership development. This person will combine:

Advanced degrees or a scientific/clinical background required.
5+ years of progressive experience in partnerships, innovative programming, grants, including relationship ownership.
Demonstrated success building and diversifying non-dues or grants revenue and converting transactional sponsorships into multi-year partnerships.
International/global experience and cultural fluency.
Fluency in healthcare funder and industry relations and the compliance environment governing industry–society relationships.
Experience building teams, systems, and pipelines from an early state.
Exceptional relationship-building, negotiation, and written/verbal communication skills.

Strategic acumen — sees the whole revenue portfolio and builds durable value, not one-off wins.

7+ years of hands-on Controllership experience in emerging growth, middle market, and/or PE-backed portfolio companies (Software/SaaS or Healthcare, or broad B2B industry exposure preferred)

Personal brand, executive presence, integrity, collaborative nature, poise and polish under pressure

Proven track record as an influential change agent, championing and successfully implementing new ideas and initiatives
Passion for mentoring and leading teams while efficiently implementing new ideas and initiatives
Identify new growth and shared revenue opportunities, collaborating with sales leadership to originate new business and grow existing relationships

Nelnet is a diversified and innovative company committed to enriching lives through the power of service as a student loan servicer, professional services company, consumer loan originator and servicer, payments processor, renewable energy solutions, and K-12 and higher education expert. For over 40 years, Nelnet has been serving its customers, associates, and communities.

The perks of working at Nelnet go beyond our benefits package. When you join the Nelnet team, you're part of a community invested in the success of each individual. That support comes through in our work, as we are united by our mission of creating opportunities for people where they live, learn, and work.

This executive role defines and owns Nelnet's collections strategy, establishing Collections Services as a scalable business line that extends consumer loan servicing across the full loan lifecycle through default resolution. The Managing Director sets the multi-year strategy, operating economics, and market positioning for recovery management and collections oversight services, deliberately positioning Nelnet as a governance and analytics provider rather than a licensed collection agency. This leader owns the collections P&L and drives revenue growth across servicing clients and prospects, NBS school partners, NFS portfolio investments, and Nelnet Bank. The role builds and leads the collections leadership team, including the Director accountable for the operating model and agency network, and represents the capability to clients, partners, and regulators. Success is measured by profitable business line ramp, client retention and wallet share, portfolio recovery improvement, and a clean regulatory and reputational record.

Define and own the multi-year collections strategy, translating market opportunity into a funded business plan, financial model, and service offering roadmap.
Own the collections services P&L, setting revenue targets, pricing and fee structures, and cost discipline to achieve breakeven and sustained profitability.
Establish the enterprise recovery management operating and governance framework, delegating build and day-to-day execution to collections leadership.

Build, lead, and develop the collections leadership team, including Directors accountable for operations, agency network, and analytics.

Report business line performance to executive leadership against financial, portfolio, client, recovery, and compliance metrics.

5+ years of P&L or business line ownership, including building a business plan and financial model from concept through revenue generation.
7+ years of accountability for third-party collection agency networks, including enterprise contract negotiation and vendor governance.
5+ years engaging executives, clients, or regulators in a regulated consumer lending or loan servicing environment.
Demonstrated success launching a new product, service line, or business competency and scaling it into an established profit center.

Experience in student loan servicing, private education lending, or bank consumer portfolios.

Experience integrating recovery performance into portfolio acquisition or investment underwriting.

new_jobs.description:
The Opportunity

Temple University Health System is seeking a physician executive to serve as Chief Executive Officer of Temple Faculty Physicians (TFP)
— the multispecialty academic practice plan through which Temple's clinical faculty deliver care across Temple Health.
The CEO is responsible for the overall leadership and performance of TFP and partners closely with the Lewis Katz School of Medicine.

About Temple Faculty Physicians

800+ physicians and advanced practice providers
across the full range of medical and surgical specialties
Care delivered at Temple University Hospital, Fox Chase Cancer Center, Jeanes Campus, Episcopal Campus, Chestnut Hill Hospital
, and ambulatory sites throughout the Philadelphia region
Physicians are dually employed by TFP and the Lewis Katz School of Medicine (LKSOM)
, holding faculty appointments while practicing through TFP
A payer mix and acuity profile that demand disciplined, creative physician enterprise leadership — and make that leadership matter

Position Summary

Reporting directly to the President & CEO of Temple University Health System
, the CEO is accountable for TFP's strategic, operational, financial, and cultural performance — clinical operations, financial results, provider compensation and workforce strategy, quality and access, and compliance.
A successful leader in this role is experienced in leading through influence and building effective partnerships with the medical school, department chairs, operational leaders, and all parts of the integrated health system.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Leadership

Develop a multi-year strategy for TFP aligned with the TUHS strategic plan and LKSOM's academic priorities
Integrate practice plan operations — payer contracting, revenue cycle, access, care standards, shared services — into the broader clinical enterprise while preserving departmental identity
Partner with system leadership on ambulatory growth, network development, service lines, and physician-facing capital investment

Academic Partnership and Governance

Establish a structured, trusted working relationship with the Dean of LKSOM, including a clear framework for joint decisions on funds flow, recruitment, effort allocation, and chair searches
Serve as the principal executive partner to clinical department chairs and co-lead the Council of Chairs
Staff the TFP board and keep governance structures current and effective

Financial Performance

Lead TFP's operating budget, multi-year financial plan, and results
Design and administer a transparent, defensible academic funds flow model
Drive revenue cycle performance and partner on payer strategy, including value-based and risk-bearing arrangements
Build provider- and department-level analytics on productivity, margin, access, and cost

Provider Recruitment, Engagement, and Retention

Oversee physician recruitment strategy jointly with chairs and the Dean's office
Champion faculty wellness, development, and retention
Make the practice plan transparent and legible to the physicians it serves
Build the next generation of physician leaders

Quality, Access, and Patient Experience

Set and achieve access targets — new patient availability, third-next-available, referral capture, continuity
Align TFP incentives to system quality and population health goals
Own patient experience performance across TFP sites
Sponsor ambulatory EHR and digital access strategy: scheduling, telehealth, messaging, provider efficiency

Operations and Organizational Development

Standardize ambulatory operations — staffing, templates, site management — where it improves performance
Develop a TFP leadership team with clear accountability and succession depth
Establish a disciplined operating rhythm with transparent scorecards and closed-loop follow-through

Qualifications

Required

MD or DO from an accredited medical or osteopathic medical school
Progressive executive leadership in a large multispecialty physician group, academic practice plan, or integrated physician enterprise, including P&L accountability
A track record of leading operational and financial improvement, integration, or large-scale change in a complex, matrixed environment
Substantive experience partnering with medical school leadership and clinical department chairs

Preferred

MBA or equivalent business credential
Experience in an academic health system serving a complex urban or safety-net population
Experience with value-based and risk-bearing contracting
Experience leading through governance transition, employment consolidation, or practice plan restructuring
Experience negotiating and administering funds flow between separately governed academic and clinical entities

About Temple Health

Temple Health is an academic health system with a deeply rooted mission: exceptional care for a community that needs it, education of the next generation of clinicians, and research that moves medicine forward. The people who thrive here are drawn to hard problems and the belief that disciplined, humane leadership changes outcomes for patients and providers alike. As CEO of TFP, you will have the platform, the partnership, and the mandate to do exactly that.

Temple Faculty Physicians, the academic practice plan of Temple Health, is made up of more than 500 employed physicians who are the cornerstone of clinical care and teaching for Temple's healthcare enterprise. These physicians practice in 20 academic departments encompassing virtually every subspecialty in modern medicine. While remaining committed to our mission of serving patients in our North Philadelphia community, in recent years, Temple Faculty Physicians has expanded its geographic reach beyond Temple University Hospital's Health Sciences campus. Today, Temple faculty physician offices are located at Temple University Hospital and its campuses, satellite offices located in Center City Philadelphia, Fort Washington, PA, Oaks, PA, and various other outpatient settings. This expanded reach has brought Temple medical care closer to home for many of our patients.

Role Overview

The Director of Strategic Partnerships & Development leads ISTH's efforts to build and diversify non-dues revenue in service of the Society's mission to advance the understanding, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment of thrombotic and bleeding disorders worldwide. Reporting to the Executive Director & CEO, the Director will design and build ISTH's strategic partnerships and development function from the ground up, spanning corporate and industry partnerships, sponsorship, education and research support, and institutional giving. The Director will cultivate durable, mission-aligned relationships across a global partner community while establishing a sustainable foundation for long-term growth.

Key Responsibilities

Strategy & Revenue Diversification

Develop and lead ISTH's strategic partnerships and revenue-diversification strategy, reducing concentration risk across partners, sectors, and revenue types.
Analyze the current revenue mix, benchmark against peer international societies, and set measurable growth and diversification targets.
Build a balanced portfolio of revenue streams impacting areas across annual congress, education, research, policy and awareness, institutional giving.

Corporate & Industry Partnerships

Design and launch a tiered Strategic Partner Program that converts episodic sponsorships into multi-year, year-round relationships.
Cultivate, negotiate, and steward partnerships across pharmaceutical, diagnostics, medical device, and digital-health sectors.
Serve as the senior relationship owner for ISTH's largest corporate partners, engaging in medical-affairs, commercial, and foundation counterparts.

Institutional Giving & Development

Establish a funding pillar including research and fellowship funds, foundation grants, and institutional giving that diversifies beyond corporate support.
Partner with foundations, and intergovernmental/NGO funders (e.g., WHO) on global health and LMIC-access programs.

Grant Writing & Proposal Development

Lead the development of high-quality grant proposals, letters of inquiry, and funding applications to foundations, corporate foundations, and other funders in support of ISTH's research, education, awareness, and global-health priorities.
Translate ISTH initiatives — fellowships, research funds, LMIC-access programs, and priority strategic initiatives — into fundable proposals tailored to each funder's mission, guidelines, and reporting expectations.
Manage the full grants lifecycle: funder prospecting and cultivation, proposal and budget development submission, and post-award stewardship and reporting, in partnership with internal departments.
Partner with program and scientific staff to source proposal content while preserving the scientific-independence firewall for funder-supported programs.

Congress Events & Sponsorships

Develop and maximize Congress-related partnership and sponsorship opportunities, including exhibition, industry-supported symposia, digital and hybrid placements, in close collaboration with the Meetings & Events team.
Develop year-round partnership opportunities around World Thrombosis Day, the Women's Health Initiative, and other mission-aligned platforms in collaboration with public affairs, marketing, education, and other relevant teams.

Compliance, Ethics & Scientific Independence

Uphold and operationalize the scientific-independence firewall so that no funder influences SSC standards, guidelines/guidance, editorial decisions, or the scientific program.
Ensure all relationships comply with the strictest applicable global transparency and disclosure regimes.
Develop and apply grant-acceptance and partner-vetting policies, escalating edge cases through the appropriate governance channels.

Team Leadership & Operations

Build and lead the Strategic Partnerships team through a phased approach aligned with revenue growth and organizational priorities; set goals, coach, and develop staff.
Stand up the function's infrastructure — database, partnership prospectus and rate card, contract and approval workflows, and reporting dashboards.
Own pipeline discipline, forecasting, and impact reporting with support from finance team; ensure relationships are held institutionally.

Advanced degrees or a scientific/clinical background required.
5+ years of progressive experience in partnerships, innovative programming, grants, including relationship ownership.
Demonstrated success building and diversifying non-dues or grants revenue and converting transactional sponsorships into multi-year partnerships.
International/global experience and cultural fluency.
Fluency in healthcare funder and industry relations and the compliance environment governing industry–society relationships.
Experience building teams, systems, and pipelines from an early state.
Exceptional relationship-building, negotiation, and written/verbal communication skills.

Core Competencies

Strategic acumen — sees the whole revenue portfolio and builds durable value, not one-off wins.
Ethical judgment & mission alignment — protects Society’s independence and reputation as the first consideration in every deal.
Relationship cultivation & stewardship — builds trust with senior partners and turns relationships into long-term, institutional commitments.
Global mindset & cultural competence — works fluently across regions, cultures, and markets in a truly international organization.
Financial literacy & data-driven decision-making — sets targets, reads the numbers, and manages a pipeline with rigor and transparency.
Team leadership & collaboration — builds and develops a team and collaborates across a matrixed, volunteer-led organization.

The ideal candidate will actively embody ISTH's core values in all aspects of leadership and decision-making.

Trust – Demonstrated integrity, transparency, and consistency in all dealings
Collaboration – Valuing diverse perspectives and partnering effectively with volunteer leadership and stakeholders
Respect – Inclusive leadership and thoughtful engagement across disciplines, regions, and backgrounds
